stem: A nurse is assessing a client for possible Parkinson disease. Which finding is most consistent with the core motor syndrome?

options.A: Progressive bradykinesia together with another parkinsonian motor feature such as rigidity or resting tremor.
options.B: Rapidly ascending symmetric weakness with areflexia and progression over days rather than a chronic parkinsonian movement pattern.
options.C: Isolated cognitive decline without bradykinesia, rigidity, resting tremor, or another progressive motor abnormality.
options.D: Sudden episodic unilateral weakness with complete recovery and no persistent or progressive movement abnormality.

rationale: NINDS describes Parkinson disease as a progressive movement disorder and lists bradykinesia, rigidity, and resting tremor among its characteristic motor manifestations. NINDS research diagnostic criteria also use bradykinesia together with at least one additional parkinsonian motor feature such as rigidity or resting tremor. A is therefore the pattern most consistent with the core motor syndrome.
educational_objective: Recognize the parkinsonian motor syndrome as progressive bradykinesia accompanied by another characteristic motor feature such as rigidity or resting tremor.
source_organization: National Institute of Neurological Disorders and Stroke (NINDS), NIH
source_version_date: Current NINDS disease page and research diagnostic criteria; live-rechecked August 16, 2026
source_locator: What is Parkinson’s disease? and motor symptom sections: progressive movement disorder with tremor, rigidity and bradykinesia. NINDS clinical-research diagnostic criteria: parkinsonian syndrome requires bradykinesia plus at least one of rigidity, rest tremor, or qualifying postural instability.
source_claim_supported: Parkinson disease produces a progressive parkinsonian motor syndrome characterized centrally by bradykinesia with other motor features such as rigidity or resting tremor.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Physiological Adaptation, printed p.14: recognize clinical manifestations and pathophysiology of chronic neurologic conditions.
blueprint_topic: Physiological Adaptation — Parkinson disease motor syndrome

correction_summary: Retained key A, added explicit NINDS diagnostic-criteria corroboration for the bradykinesia-plus-another-motor-feature structure, and set difficulty to medium because the final item requires syndrome-level discrimination rather than recall of a single symptom.

audit_findings.source_authority: NINDS/NIH disease page and NINDS research diagnostic criteria; NCSBN 2026 Test Plan
audit_findings.exact_locator: NINDS What is PD?/motor symptoms and research criteria requiring bradykinesia plus another parkinsonian feature
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item identifies a syndrome pattern rather than claiming the listed signs alone definitively diagnose idiopathic PD.

distractor_audit.B: Incorrect; describes an acute ascending peripheral weakness syndrome rather than parkinsonism.
distractor_audit.C: Incorrect; isolated cognitive decline without motor parkinsonism does not fit the core motor syndrome.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect; transient focal weakness is not the progressive movement pattern of PD.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A contains the progressive parkinsonian motor pattern.
audit_findings.cueing: All options describe neurologic patterns and require syndrome discrimination.
audit_findings.blueprint: Physiological Adaptation — chronic neurologic disease manifestations.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Re-read NINDS disease and research diagnostic criteria, all options, rationale and NCSBN mapping. A remained uniquely correct.
